stem: Why can a daily environmental average be insufficient for some troubleshooting tasks?
choices: Daily averages exaggerate every short-term peak, so they should be avoided in troubleshooting.
A daily average contains too little numerical information to support any environmental interpretation.
Short excursions, transitions, and equipment-cycling patterns can be hidden when many readings are compressed into one average.
A single instantaneous reading is always more useful than an average because it preserves exact conditions.
rationale: Averages are useful for summary, but they can hide when and how strongly conditions moved outside the normal pattern. Short spikes, cycling faults, light-on/light-off transitions, or irrigation-linked changes may disappear inside a daily mean. Troubleshooting often requires both the average and the underlying time-series or event context.
